enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1131 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1125 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

 - A brief stretch of drier weather today and Wednesday before 
   rain chances return Thursday through the weekend. A few storms 
   will be capable of heavy rain and localized flooding.

 - Typical temperatures for the end of October with lowland highs
   in the mid to upper 70s, becoming slightly cooler this 
   weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1125 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Water vapor satellite imagery shows broad but low-amplitude
troughing over the Western half or so of the CONUS. Flow is
relatively weak over us with plenty of dry air aloft though
surface moisture remains seasonably robust with dew points in the
upper 40s to upper 50s east. A weak system is departing the area.
With a lack of UL forcing, nearly all of us are expected to stay
dry this afternoon. The exception will be toward the Hudspeth -
Culberson County line as storms are expected to fire in that
vicinity. Temperatures will be seasonable. We will see very
similar conditions for tomorrow with a degree or two of warming.
GFS and HRRR continue to show a single for isolated storms across
Hudspeth County (farther west in the GFS), so I added low POPs for
that area. Most of us remain dry. 

Our next UL system begins to affect the area on Thursday. A s/w
trough will strengthen off the Baja Coast before shifting ENE. 
This pattern will draw moisture into Southern NM and Far West TX 
while UL support increases. Thus, showers and thunderstorms will 
develop/move north, with at least scattered coverage anticipated 
by Thursday afternoon into the overnight hours. We will see a 
quick break with this activity as the initial trough axis passes 
followed by a very small S/W ridge. This break does not last long 
though as another ripple quickly follows Friday afternoon into 
early Saturday morning with more showers and thunderstorms 
anticipated. For both days, modest CAPE (~500 J/kg) and shear (~20
knots; slightly higher on Friday) should preclude a severe 
weather risk based on the LREF mean though it should be noted the 
Euro shows a little stronger CAPE (closer to 1000 J/kg) and shear 
(near 30 knots) for Thursday, which would lend to a non-zero 
severe threat. Heavy rainfall and isolated flash flooding will be 
the main concerns for Thursday and Friday.

We get a break for Halloween. The second ripple will be exiting
the area taking precip chances with it by day break with a s/w
ridge building in its wake. The rest of the day will feature 
clearing with temperatures near normal. There will be nothing 
spooky about the forecast that evening. 

The Halloween ridge clears out quickly, and our next system begins
pushing into the area starting Sunday ahead of a large S/W trough 
off the SoCal Coast as eastern AZ and western NM enter the exit 
region of the low's jet. Rain chances will slowly overspread the 
area from west to east beginning early Sunday morning for the AZ- 
NM border, reaching the eastern extent of our CWA by Sunday night.
Rain will be more stratiform with this event (isolated thunder), 
so the risk for severe will be none and flooding very low. This 
system will clear out sometime Monday, taking rain chances with 
it. It will also push a Pacific front through the area, and 
temperatures will be below normal by the start of next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1125 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

VFR conditions expected with SKC to few clouds at various heights.
Winds will be light and variable though generally favoring the S
or SE.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1125 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast for the period as afternoon
RH values stay well above critical thresholds with light winds.
Temperatures will be seasonal. Little to no rain chances are
forecast for today and tomorrow, but widespread showers and 
thunderstorms are in the forecast for Thursday, Friday, and 
Sunday. Vent rates will range poor to good each afternoon. The 
weakest vent rates will be Thursday and Friday.
